### Investment Memo: EQX — November 12, 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD — with a Reduce/Underweight bias (do not add; new money waits for defined triggers) | Conviction: **Medium**
**Price Target**: **$11.00** (~6% upside from current $10.39) — probability-weighted; scenario range $8.25–$16.50
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**
EQX is a transformed ~1.1Moz gold producer with a genuinely repaired balance sheet (net debt $1.4B → net cash, $1.2B liquidity) and record revenue and EBITDA — but it remains a high-cost (AISC ~$2,000–2,100/oz vs. ~$1,785 industry average), high-beta (2.2–2.5 vs. SPY, 1.15 vs. GDX) gold proxy whose shareholders have captured essentially none of the greatest gold bull market in history: operating cash flow per share went from $1.13 (2021) to $1.11 (2025) while gold rose 89%, with five consecutive negative-FCF years and +310% dilution. At $10.39 the market is paying fair value for ~$4,000 gold with zero margin of safety, into a hawkish Fed and a negatively-skewed Feb-17 print, while ~15–33% of output sits in sanctions-exposed Nicaragua. There is no fraud and no solvency risk — but also no stock-specific edge (1-yr alpha vs. GDX −16.8%, R² 0.85).

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Sector rated Attractive (record AISC margins, 12% earnings yield, cheapest vs. S&P in 20 years) but late-cycle — prefer low-cost majors over EQX within it. Macro Neutral with negative skew: 10Y TIPS at a 2.66% cycle high, a 78%-priced Dec-9 hike, gold −27% from peak at ~$4,013, WTI ~$100 (+43%) inflating AISC. Every *marginal* macro variable is moving against the stock; BRL/MXN weakness partially cushions USD unit costs.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **HIGH**, improving. Nicaragua (15–18% of revenue; live OFAC escalation, state seizure precedent) plus Mexico (Los Filos 18-month suspension, permit freeze; June-26 land agreements signed) put roughly a third of revenue in jurisdictions where the state, not courts, determines outcomes. A Brazilian court blocking the CMOC mineral-rights transfer threatens the $115M contingent payment due Jan-2027.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: Moat **NONE** — a price-taker with no cost advantage. Critical correction: post-Orla share count is ~1.16–1.25B, so market cap is **~$12.1B, not the stale $6.5B** in vendor screens; the "cheap" headline multiples were a share-count artifact. Corrected EV/EBITDA ≈ 8x LTM and 5.7x 2027E — but ~10.5x on mid-cycle ($3,500) gold, i.e. a *premium* to its own history once earnings normalize.

Upgrade trigger: two quarters of per-ounce margin expansion with flat share count; downgrade: Q4 <870koz or AISC >$1,800.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **SELL** — worst-in-cohort value (5/100) and quality (5/100), ROIC 6.0% vs. ~9% WACC (economic value destruction), 65% vol, raw 12-1 momentum −21%, and near-zero two-year alpha vs. GDX: a levered beta certificate, not a mispricing.
- **Financial Risk**: **MODERATE**. Credit risk genuinely low — net cash, ~4x interest coverage through a −20% gold shock, no maturity wall. But market risk is high (−54% drawdown Feb→Jul 2026), FCF quality poor (~1% yield; $640–700M/yr capex consumes nearly all operating cash flow), and working capital deteriorating (current ratio 0.93). The real break point is gold ~$2,450, not the balance sheet at current prices.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **HIGH**. Two mergers plus CEO *and* Chair turnover inside 13 months (the ex-Orla team now runs the company — a de facto reverse takeover of management); Los Filos is a repeat-failure social-licence problem; Q4 needs a record ~258koz. Meaningful offset: unambiguous insider buying (Beaty ~C$9.7M in Aug-26 after ~US$18.2M earlier; zero selling into the drawdown).
- **ESG**: **AVERAGE / Neutral**. Zero fatalities and zero significant environmental incidents in 2025; majority Tier-1 jurisdiction mix post-Brazil exit. But Los Filos represents ~$300–380M/yr of forgone EBITDA (the largest ESG-attributable loss in the file), there is a fresh serious-injury OHS probe at Valentine, and governance scores 5/10 after serial M&A and CEO churn.

Stock −14.1% vs. GDX −9.5% post-print: trust the tape, not the +0.60 sentiment score. Washed-out positioning (search interest −83% from peak) is constructive on a 12-month view.

The bear case is capital allocation, not integrity: cumulative FCF −$735M (2021–25) and 45% of Q2-26 EPS from non-operating items. But net cash, a rising dividend, and a 2.5 beta make a naked short a widow-maker into any gold re-acceleration.

**Data integrity & disagreement flags**: (1) Nicaragua exposure is 15–18% of revenue (Geo-Legal) vs. 33% of YTD output (Non-Financial — production-based, post-Brazil, likely more current); (2) "AISC" figures range $1,605–$2,175 across reports due to cash-cost/AISC and period definitional mix — I use ~$2,000–2,100 (Q3-26: $2,091, −4% QoQ); (3) net cash is $16M–$214M depending on convert treatment; (4) vendor multiples are contaminated by the stale 630M share count.

- **Debasement decoupling**: if gold re-takes $5,000 on fiscal-dominance repricing (Macro: 25–30% probability), 2.3x realised beta plus a net-cash balance sheet supports **$15–18** (+45–75%).
- **Self-help re-rate**: cash costs −9% and AISC −4% QoQ; Greenstone/Valentine hitting nameplate plus a full year of Orla and South Railroad first gold (2028) on the path toward 2Moz; any AISC guide below ~$1,700 is a re-rating trigger.
- **Insider conviction + capital returns**: founder buying aggressively below the current price; dividend raised 50%, buyback initiated, $1.2B liquidity — per-share discipline is finally visible.

**Bear Case**

- **Q4 miss**: a record quarter is required against two underperforming Canadian ramps and Mesquite pit instability; consensus revenue/EPS look 8–9% high — the Feb-17 print skews negative (Alt Data).
- **Binary jurisdictional tail**: ~15–33% of output in Nicaragua with no disclosed mitigation or divestiture path, plus Los Filos repeat-failure risk — unhedgeable and not priced as binary.

**Key Risks**
Gold price (~90% of the thesis; beta 2.2–2.5); Nicaragua sanctions escalation; Feb-17 guidance miss; resumption of equity-funded growth capex; energy-driven AISC inflation (WTI +43%); Mexico open-pit ban bill and PROFEPA closures; Brazil $115M receivable; data-integrity caveats above.

**Portfolio Construction Note** (Portfolio Strategist)
**0% — Pass at $10.39.** Probability-weighted expected return is ~+5% on 65% volatility (Sharpe ~0.08) after the Nicaragua tail haircut — below the threshold to move a diversified book. EQX–GDX correlation of 0.92 with −16.8% alpha means it adds beta and tail risk, not return; express constructive gold views through **GDX or AEM/NEM** instead. Pre-committed entry triggers: **(A)** post-Feb-17 capitulation below ~$8.50 with FY27 guidance ≥1.05Moz and AISC ≤$2,000/oz → initiate 0.75–1.0%; **(B)** an announced Nicaragua divestiture → ~1%+ (strategist's report truncated at the exact figure). Existing holders: hold, size strictly as gold beta, do not add above $12.

# Portfolio Construction Recommendation — EQX (Equinox Gold Corp.)
**Price $10.39 (12-Nov-26 close) · Market cap ~$12.1bn (1.16bn sh) · ADV ~$130m**

> **Data-integrity note up front.** The valuation tools returned a $6.55bn market cap on 630.3m shares — a stale pre-Orla count. Post-Orla (31-Jul-26) the register is ~1,167.5m basic / 1,247.5m fully diluted, so market cap is **~$12.1bn**, not $6.55bn. The tool's P/E 28.9x, P/B 1.13x, EV/EBITDA 8.94x and P/FCF −978x are all contaminated. Corrected on LTM adjusted EBITDA (~$1.5bn, net cash): **EV/EBITDA ≈ 8.0x LTM → 5.7x 2027E → ~10.5x on mid-cycle gold.** I flag this because the Quant's "15.6x pro-forma" applies the right EV to a stale FY25 EBITDA and the Sector/Growth "cheap at 8x" applies LTM EBITDA to peak-cycle earnings. Both are half-right; my reconstruction is below.

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector Researcher** | Neutral on EQX / Attractive sector | **High** | AISC $1,900–2,000/oz vs $1,785 industry; 10–20pt EBITDA margin gap to majors; −4% 12-mo vs NEM +41%. Prefers AEM/NEM/B/KGC within the sector. |
| **Geo Legal** | **Negative** | **High** | **HIGH** risk rating. Nicaragua ~15–18% of revenue with live OFAC escalation (Apr-26 tranche); Mexico permitting freeze + blockade history; Brazilian court blocking mineral-rights transfer, $115m receivable at risk. Improving trend. |
| **Macro** | **Neutral, negative skew** | **Medium** | 10Y TIPS at 2.66% cycle high; 78% odds of a 9-Dec hike; WTI $100 (+43%); USD +3.4%. Gold −27% from peak. Bull $16–18 (25–30%), bear $8.00–8.50 (30%). |
| **Value** | **Negative** | **Medium-High** | Moat **NONE**; correct market cap is $12.1bn not $6.5bn — the "cheap" screen is a 2x error. DCF tool fails outright on negative base FCF. |
| **Growth** | **Hold** | **Medium** | Balance sheet transformation real (net cash), $2,700/oz cash margin — but Rule of 40 = 22, revenue/share +19% vs +97% headline, 130% dilution, gross margin 50.9%→39.2%→**33.7%** sequentially. EPS peaks 2028 in consensus. |
| **Fin Risk** | **Moderate** | **High** | Credit **low** (net cash, ~4x coverage through a −20% gold shock, no maturity wall); market risk **high** (65% vol, 2.2 beta, −54% DD); FCF quality weak (~1% yield); current ratio 1.56→**0.93**. |
| **Nonfin Risk** | **Negative** | **High** | **HIGH**. Nicaragua ~33% of YTD output (company flags sanctions as a risk factor); Los Filos suspended 18 months w/ failed social licence; 2 mergers + CEO/Chair turnover in 13 months; Q4 needs a record 258.5koz. Offset: heavy insider buying. |
| **Quant** | **SELL** | **High** | Worst-in-cohort Value (5/100) and Quality (5/100); **alpha vs GDX −16.8%, R² 0.85, beta 1.15** → no stock-specific edge, pure miner-complex beta at a cohort-max multiple. |
| **Short Analyst** | **Bearish tilt / NO EDGE** | **High** | **No fraud** — Beneish −2.64, accruals −4.5%, receivables shrinking. But cumulative FCF −$735m (2021–25) and **OCF/share flat ($1.13→$1.11) through an 89% gold rally**. Naked short rejected. |
| **ESG** | **Neutral** | **Medium** | AVERAGE (weak on Social). Los Filos = ~$300–380m/yr forgone EBITDA. Governance 5/10. No forced-seller dynamic, no uninsurable tail. |
| **Alt Data** | **Bearish (mild), catalyst-dated** | **Medium** | Consensus Q4 rev $1.18bn looks **8–9% too high**; EPS $0.34 requires +79% QoQ. Sentiment score +0.60 but stock −14.1% vs GDX −9.5% post-print — **trust the tape**. |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** (directionally negative, with three high-confidence anchors)

Agreement is **low on valuation, high on risk**. Three blocks are near-unanimous and should carry full weight:

- **Block A — the balance sheet repair is real (11/11 agree, zero dissent).** Net debt $1.4bn → net cash ($16–214m depending on definition), $1.2bn liquidity, converts called. Credit risk is genuinely resolved. *This is not the issue.*
- **Block B — shareholders have captured none of the gold bull market (Growth, Short, Quant, Value concur; Short's evidence is decisive).** OCF/share $1.13 (2021) → $1.11 (2025) against gold +89%. Five straight negative-FCF years. Dilution +310%. This is the single most damaging fact in the file and no agent rebuts it.
- **Block C — the jurisdiction tail is binary and unhedgeable (Geo, Nonfin, ESG concur; magnitudes conflict).** Note the disagreement: Geo says Nicaragua is 15–18% of revenue, Nonfin says **33% of YTD output**. Nonfin's figure is post-Brazil-sale and production-based, so it is the current one. Either way it is a single-jurisdiction, single-policy-event exposure with no disclosed mitigation structure or divestiture path. **Per my framework, a binary structural risk of this kind takes precedence over a valuation discount.**

Where agents genuinely **conflict**, I resolve as follows:

| Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Sector/Growth: "8x EV/EBITDA, clear discount to NEM/AEM double digits" vs Quant: "actually 15.6x, more expensive than cohort" | **Both wrong, and it matters.** Corrected: ~8.0x LTM, **5.7x 2027E**, but **~10.5x on mid-cycle ($3,500) gold**. The discount is a peak-earnings artifact, not a durable value gap. On mid-cycle the stock is at a *premium* to its own history. |
| Value/Quant: "most expensive in cohort" vs Short: "7.5x 2027E is cheap if gold holds" | Both describe the same object from different gold prices. **The entire valuation question collapses to a gold-price call**, which is Macro's mandate — and Macro is Neutral with negative skew. |
| Alt Data bearish into 17-Feb vs Nonfin bullish (Beaty: 600k shares @ C$9.66m + 22.5m shares) | Different horizons, not different facts. Insider buying is a 2–3 year signal; the Q4 print is a 3-month risk. Both can be true. |
| Short: "no fraud" vs the bear case generally | **The fraud override does NOT apply.** Accounting is clean. This is a capital-allocation and cycle-position problem, not an integrity problem — which caps how negative one can responsibly be. |

**Structural read:** EQX is not a stock with idiosyncratic mispricing. It is a **1.15x levered GDX certificate with negative alpha and a sanctions tail attached.** Eight of eleven agents independently describe the same object: a high-beta, high-cost, serial-diluting gold proxy whose price is fair for the gold price that prevails today.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **0.0% — Pass**

**My reconstructed intrinsic value bridge** (1.1Moz, AISC ~$2,000/oz, 1.16bn sh):

| Gold | Margin/oz | EBITDA | EPS | Fair value @ 10–12x | vs $10.39 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $5,000 | $3,000 | ~$3.0bn | ~$1.35 | **$15–18** | +45–73% |
| $4,500 | $2,500 | ~$2.75bn | ~$1.21 | **$13–14** | +25–35% |
| **$4,000** | $2,000 | ~$2.2bn | **~$0.88** | **$10.50–11** | **≈ fair** |
| $3,600 | $1,600 | ~$1.76bn | ~$0.60 | $6–7 | −35% |
| $3,300 | $1,300 | ~$1.4bn | ~$0.38 | $4–5 | −55% |

**The stock at $10.39 is priced at fair value for $4,000 gold — with zero margin of safety.** The −44% drawdown from $18.88 is *beta working as designed*, not a mispricing: EQX fell 54% on a 24% gold decline (2.3x realised downside beta, confirmed by calculated beta 2.21 and the Quant's 1.15x GDX beta). Buying "down 45%" buys nothing unless you hold a differentiated gold view.

**Kelly check:** probability-weighted return = 0.275×(+65%) + 0.425×(−8%) + 0.30×(−20%) = **+8.5%**, less a ~12% probability-weighted Nicaragua tail of −30% (≈ −3.6%) → **~+5% expected return on 65% volatility = Sharpe ~0.08.** Kelly fraction ≈ edge/variance ≈ 0.05/0.42 ≈ **12% of a fully-risky slug**, then haircut ~75% for fat tails, unhedgeable jurisdiction risk, and negative alpha vs benchmark. That lands at **≤0.5–1%**, i.e. below the threshold where position size can move a diversified book.

**Sizing conclusion: 0% now.** A 0.5% position would be a rounding error that adds 65%-vol exposure, a sanctions tail, and 0.92 correlation to any gold sleeve already held — you pay idiosyncratic risk without collecting idiosyncratic return (alpha vs GDX is **−16.8%**).

**If the PM overrides and requires exposure:** maximum **0.5%**, no more, and express it as a *gold-beta* position, not a value position.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector/concentration — adds nothing.** Basic Materials. EQX is a $12.1bn company in a sector where the top-5 names are $88–242bn. Any existing gold or materials sleeve makes this 100% redundant.

**Correlation — this is the disqualifying metric:**

| Pair | Correlation | Read |
|---|---|---|
| EQX–GDX | **0.919** | 85% of variance is the miner complex. Zero diversification. |
| EQX–AEM | 0.896 | Indistinguishable from the senior you'd rather own |
| EQX–GLD | 0.821 | Levered gold, nothing more |
| EQX–SPY | 0.488 | Only apparent "diversifier" — and that's the beta, not a benefit |

**Factor exposure — accretive in the wrong direction.** EQX is a negative loading on every factor that works: worst-in-cohort Value (5/100), worst-in-cohort Quality (5/100 — ROIC 6.0% vs ~9% WACC, i.e. **destroying economic value**), high-vol (65% ann., 2.2 beta vs SPY), and raw 12-1 momentum **−21.3%** (the tool's +7.9% is unverified and contradicted by the raw price series). Adding EQX increases portfolio beta, increases volatility, lowers portfolio quality, and adds a name with no momentum support. It is an **anti-factor position**.

**Liquidity — not a constraint.** ~12–15m shares/day (~$130m). Any position we could justify sizes in one day.

**Portfolio-level verdict:** If the house view is constructive on gold, the correct expression is **GDX (diversified, no single-jurisdiction tail) or AEM/NEM (lower cost, Tier-1 jurisdictions, positive relative momentum)**. Owning EQX to express a gold view means paying a 12-month −16.8% alpha penalty and accepting a ~33%-of-output sanctions tail in exchange for leverage you can replicate with index futures or GDX calls at defined risk.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy — **No entry at $10.39. Pre-committed triggers only.**

Do **not** scale in here. The setup is: a hard, dated, negatively-skewed catalyst 3 months out (17-Feb-27, consensus EPS $0.34 / rev $1.18bn vs Alt Data's bottom-up 8–9% below), a Fed decision on 9-Dec (78% hike), and a stock that just fell 14% in three sessions while the tape leads the sentiment score. Buying into that is buying a coin flip with negative expectancy on the near term.

**Define the entry in advance — either trigger is sufficient:**

- **Trigger A (capitulation + guidance intact):** post-17-Feb print, price **< $8.50** *and* FY2027 guidance ≥1.05Moz with AISC ≤$2,000/oz, *and* FCF positive. Initiate **0.75–1.0%**. That price implies the market is discounting ~$3,600 gold — which is Macro's bear case already paid for.
- **Trigger B (tail removed):** announced **sale or spin of the Nicaraguan assets** at any reasonable price. This converts ~33% of output from binary to priced and would justify **1.

# Sector Brief — Gold Mining (Basic Materials) | Target: Equinox Gold Corp. (EQX)

*Data note: latest full-year financials are FY2025 (Dec-31-2025); quarterly data through Q3 2026 (Sept-30-2026, reported Nov-9-2026). Prices as of Nov-12-2026. Margin comparisons are on reported (FMP-standardised) gross/operating lines; D&A sits inside cost of revenue for all names, but D&A intensity differs materially, so operating margins understate EQX's relative position less than they appear — see EBITDA note.*

---

## 1. Sector Overview

Gold mining is a ~3,600–3,700t/yr primary-supply industry with structurally inelastic supply: 10–15 year permitting/development lead times, declining reserve grades, and reserve depletion at the majors (Newmont's attributable reserves fell from 134.1Moz to 118.2Moz in 2025). Production is fragmented at the asset level but the corporate tier is consolidating — 2025–26 saw Newmont/Goldcorp-style logic repeated via Barrick–Newmont's Nevada Gold Mines JV expansion ($1.95bn consideration to Barrick) and mid-tier mergers such as Equinox's combination with Orla. Crucially, 2026 is a **record-margin year**: spot gold printed an all-time high of ~$5,595/oz in January 2026 and traded $4,500–4,900 through Q2, while global average AISC rose only to **$1,785/oz in Q1'26** (+5% q/q, +16% y/y) — pushing average AISC margins to a record **~$3,076/oz (+134% y/y)**. The sector's Basic Materials aggregate (22 largest names, FY2025) shows $484bn revenue, $159bn gross profit (32.9%) and $70.6bn net income (14.6% net margin). The sector is **late-cycle on margins, mid-cycle on volume** — the profit pool is expanding because of price, not ounces.

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Record price-to-cost spread.** Average AISC $1,785/oz (Q1'26) against gold averaging >$4,500/oz implies ~60–70% cash margins per ounce — the widest in the industry's history. Every $100/oz on gold is worth roughly $90–95m of EBITDA to EQX on ~0.9Moz+ guidance.
- **Structural, price-insensitive demand.** Central-bank accumulation, ETF re-stocking and debasement/rate-cut logic; sell-side targets cluster at $4,275/oz (Reuters poll average for 2026) to $4,650/oz (Goldman, end-2026). BofA notes gold miners' **earnings yield of 12.0% is the highest of any sector** and the cheapest vs the S&P 500 in 20 years — a valuation tailwind for the whole peer group.
- **Consolidation and capital returns.** Majors are buying growth rather than building it (Nevada JV restructuring), which supports takeout premia for mid-tiers with permitted pipelines. Sector balance sheets have delevered and dividends/buybacks are now normal (EQX initiated and has since raised its dividend, returning $35m in Q3'26 alone).

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **28 consecutive quarters of AISC inflation.** Costs are ratcheting: royalties have doubled from ~6% to ~12% of AISC since Q1'21, with **sliding-scale royalty regimes** introduced in Ghana (up to 12% above $4,500/oz), Burkina Faso (10%), and Mali (9.5%) — a direct tax on the price rally, and EQX's Brazil/Mexico exposure carries similar resource-nationalism risk.
- **Energy and supply-chain shock.** Closure of the Strait of Hormuz drove US diesel +54% q/q and Perth wholesale diesel +96% in Q1'26. Large caps are hedged (Newmont, Evolution, OceanaGold report PPAs/fuel contracts); **junior and mid-tier producers are structurally more exposed** — a relative disadvantage for EQX.
- **Margin mean-reversion and M&A overpayment risk.** If gold normalises toward $3,500–4,000/oz, the sector's record margins compress violently because AISC is sticky downward. Reserve depletion plus a bidding war for quality ounces also raises the risk of value-destructive deals; EQX's own all-share Orla transaction lifted the share count from ~630m to ~1.04bn, diluting per-share leverage to gold.

## 4. Peer Comparison Table (FY2025, USD)

| Company | Revenue | Rev YoY | Gross mgn | Op. mgn | 12-mo price (to 12-Nov-26) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EQX (Equinox Gold)** | $1.85bn | +22.1% | 25.0% | 23.8% | **−3.8%** ($10.80→$10.39) |
| NEM (Newmont) | $22.67bn | +22.2% | 53.2% | 48.6% | **+41.3%** |
| AEM (Agnico Eagle) | $11.91bn | +43.7% | 58.1% | 53.1% | +12.3% |
| B (Barrick Mining) | $16.96bn | +31.2% | 51.3% | 47.8% | n/a |
| KGC (Kinross) | $7.17bn | +39.3% | 47.5% | 43.2% | n/a |
| AU (AngloGold) | $9.89bn | +70.8% | 46.5% | 45.1% | n/a |
| **Peer median (ex-EQX)** | $13.4bn* | **+39.3%** | **51.3%** | **47.8%** | +26.8%* |
| Basic Materials aggregate (22 cos) | $484.1bn | — | 32.9% | — | — |

\*Median of B/AU = $13.4bn; 12-mo price median of NEM/AEM only.

**EQX (quarterly run-rate, 2026):** Q1 rev $861.6m / EBITDA $461.8m (53.6%); Q2 rev $769.8m / EBITDA $448.0m (58.2%); Q3 rev $1,029.4m (record) / EBITDA **$433.2m (42.1%)**, net income only $67.5m on $30.8m interest and step-up D&A. 9M-2026 revenue of $2.66bn already exceeds FY2025 by 44%; FY2026 revenue should land near $3.5bn (~+90% y/y), almost entirely from the Orla consolidation rather than organic ounces.

**Verdict on benchmarking:** EQX wins on *reported* growth but loses decisively on *quality* of margin — ~42–46% EBITDA margin vs an estimated 55–65% for the majors, i.e. a 10–20pt gap that is a genuine cost-curve issue, not just accounting. EQX's 2026 AISC guidance of **$1,900–2,000/oz sits 6–12% above the $1,785/oz industry average**. It also conspicuously failed to participate in the sector re-rating: NEM +41%, AEM +12% versus EQX −4% over twelve months, and EQX is ~45% below its February 2026 high of $18.86 (drawdown to $8.61 in July).

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **Average** (improving, with execution risk)

**Interest rates & real yields — NEGATIVE (dominant variable).**

Gold is a genuine inflation hedge and 3.8% CPI supports the structural bid, but the *composition* of this inflation is hostile: it is energy-led, and energy is a direct input to mining.
